option_description: Whether the running NGFW firmware is at or below a release affected by a publicly-known, CISA-KEV-listed pre-auth RCE/auth-bypass CVE (e.g. PAN-OS GlobalProtect CVE-2024-3400, FortiOS SSL-VPN CVE-2024-21762) and not yet at the vendor fixed release.
security_impact: References the exposure "Unpatched firmware pre-auth RCE on exposed VPN/portal service" — it is the is_true OR-trigger of that exposure's first AND-group (paired with vpn_portal_service_internet_exposed), firing T1190 / T1542.002 when the appliance runs vulnerable firmware reachable on an internet-facing service.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running firmware version and compare it against the vendor fixed-release advisories for every KEV-listed edge CVE (PAN-OS/FortiOS), within CISA BOD 22-01 remediation deadlines.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Firmware version is at/above the fixed release for any KEV-listed edge CVE (PAN-OS/FortiOS) within CISA BOD 22-01 remediation deadlines. TRUE (insecure) when at/below a vulnerable build.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On FortiGate, read the running firmware build; on PAN-OS read the running software version, then map to the fixed-release advisories.
how_to_obtain.command: get system status   # FortiOS; PAN-OS: show system info | match sw-version
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version string (e.g. FortiOS v7.x build, or PAN-OS 11.1.2-h3) that an assessor checks against CVE-2024-3400 / CVE-2024-21762 fixed releases.

option_description: Whether the appliance's internet-facing pre-auth services — GlobalProtect gateway/portal (PAN-OS) or SSL-VPN/sslvpnd (FortiOS) — accept connections from untrusted/internet zones.
security_impact: Necessary second AND-condition of the exposure "Unpatched firmware pre-auth RCE on exposed VPN/portal service" — appears (is_true) in BOTH of that exposure's AND-groups; without internet reachability the firmware flaw is not remotely exploitable (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an untrusted/internet source range, probe the GlobalProtect portal/gateway (TCP 443) or FortiOS SSL-VPN listener and confirm whether it answers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: the VPN/portal port is filtered/closed from untrusted ranges (behind a VPN-broker). TRUE (insecure) when the portal/SSL-VPN responds to internet sources.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect which interface/zone the SSL-VPN / GlobalProtect listener is bound to and whether that interface faces untrusted zones.
how_to_obtain.command: show system interface <external-interface>   # FortiOS; PAN-OS: review GlobalProtect gateway interface/zone binding
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SSL-VPN/GlobalProtect bound only to interfaces not reachable from internet/untrusted source ranges.
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

option_description: Whether the edge appliance firmware (FortiOS/FortiProxy/PAN-OS) is patched to the vendor fixed release within the remediation SLA (e.g. CISA BOD 22-01 KEV deadlines). Read with is_false.
security_impact: Read is_false in TWO exposures: it is the second AND-group's patch-currency trigger of "Unpatched firmware pre-auth RCE on exposed VPN/portal service" (paired with vpn_portal_service_internet_exposed), and an OR-trigger of "Management-plane authentication bypass" (CVE-2022-40684 exists only on unpatched firmware). Fires when the appliance is NOT patched within SLA.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the firmware is at/above the vendor fixed release for all applicable KEV CVEs and that the patch was applied within the organisation's remediation SLA.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Firmware version is at/above the fixed release for any KEV-listed edge CVE (PAN-OS/FortiOS) within CISA BOD 22-01 remediation deadlines. is_false (insecure) when not patched within SLA.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm the update path is healthy so patches can be applied promptly: verify update-server identity and that content auto-install is scheduled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Device > Dynamic Updates / Device > Setup > Services (Verify Update Server Identity)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.6.1 'Verify Update Server Identity' checked; CIS 4.1/4.2 AV and Applications-and-Threats set to Download and Install on a frequent schedule (Palo Alto).

option_description: Whether the firewall's administrative/management interface (FortiGate allowaccess https/ssh on an external interface, or a PAN-OS mgmt profile without a restrictive permitted-IP list) is reachable from untrusted/internet source ranges.
security_impact: An is_true OR-trigger of the exposure "Management-plane authentication bypass" — it is the precondition that turns a management-plane auth-bypass flaw (CVE-2022-40684) into a remotely exploitable admin takeover (T1190 / T1562.013).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the allowaccess list on the internet-facing FortiGate interface and confirm admin protocols are not exposed there.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: allowaccess on internet-facing interface does NOT include https/ssh/http/telnet; admin access only on mgmt interface (FortiGate).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm admin accounts restrict source IPs so even a reachable interface only accepts mgmt subnets.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each admin has trustedhost1..N set to specific mgmt subnets (e.g. 172.25.176.0/24); empty/0.0.0.0/0 trustedhost is insecure (FortiGate).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm Permitted IP Addresses are set on every interface-mgmt profile that enables SSH/HTTPS/SNMP.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Network > Network Profiles > Interface Mgmt (Permitted IP Addresses per profile)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.2.1/1.2.2: 'Permitted IP Addresses' set on every interface-mgmt profile where SSH/HTTPS/SNMP is enabled, restricted to mgmt addresses only (Palo Alto).

option_description: Whether the device's control-plane/management API (the HTTP/HTTPS admin endpoint a bypass request targets) is NOT exposed to public/untrusted networks. Secure value is TRUE.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Management-plane authentication bypass" — when the API is publicly exposed (FALSE), a crafted-request authentication bypass becomes reachable by an unauthenticated remote attacker (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an untrusted source range, probe the management/control-plane HTTPS API port and confirm it does not answer.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: the control-plane API port is filtered/closed from untrusted ranges. is_false (insecure) when the admin API responds to public sources.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the allowaccess/mgmt-profile binding so the admin HTTPS endpoint listens only on management interfaces.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: allowaccess on internet-facing interface does NOT include https/ssh/http/telnet; admin access only on mgmt interface (FortiGate).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

option_description: Whether edge-appliance management interfaces (HTTPS/SSH/SNMP admin, GUI, CLI) are not reachable from the internet — segmented behind a management network/jump host and source-IP restricted. Secure value is TRUE.
security_impact: Read is_false as an OR-trigger of TWO exposures: "Management-plane authentication bypass" and "Internet-exposed management plane with default or weak admin credentials". When FALSE the management plane is internet-reachable and exploitable by the auth bypass or default-credential attack (T1190 / T1133).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify admin access is bound to a dedicated management interface and that the internet-facing interface's allowaccess excludes admin protocols.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: allowaccess on internet-facing interface does NOT include https/ssh/http/telnet; admin access only on mgmt interface (FortiGate).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm Permitted IP Addresses on each mgmt profile restrict admin access to management subnets only.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Network > Network Profiles > Interface Mgmt (Permitted IP Addresses per profile)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.2.1/1.2.2: 'Permitted IP Addresses' set on every interface-mgmt profile where SSH/HTTPS/SNMP is enabled, restricted to mgmt addresses only (Palo Alto).

option_description: Whether all vendor default admin accounts/passwords (e.g. admin/admin) have been changed, renamed, or disabled so no account uses a publicly-known default credential.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Internet-exposed management plane with default or weak admin credentials" — when vendor defaults remain in use (FALSE), default-credential brute-force/guessing of the management plane succeeds (T1110 / T1133).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate admin accounts and confirm none retain a vendor default credential and default accounts are renamed/disabled; attempt the vendor default login and confirm it fails.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No account uses a vendor default password; default 'admin' login fails. Vendor defaults favor ease-of-use over security and must be removed.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 4 — Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software

how_to_obtain.instruction: List configured admin accounts on FortiGate to check for the default 'admin' account.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Admin account list shows the default 'admin' renamed/disabled and no account with a default password (FortiGate).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

option_description: Whether multi-factor/two-factor authentication (FortiToken / RADIUS+OTP, or a PAN-OS MFA-backed authentication profile) is available and enforced for privileged admin logins.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Internet-exposed management plane with default or weak admin credentials" — single-factor password-only login (FALSE) leaves no second factor to resist credential theft/guessing on the management plane (T1110 / T1133).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read admin account config and confirm two-factor is enabled on privileged admins.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: two-factor enabled on admin accounts (FortiGate supports FortiToken / FortiToken Mobile two-factor).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm an MFA-backed authentication profile is enforced for all privileged admin logins (FortiToken, or RADIUS/TACACS+ with OTP on PAN-OS).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every privileged admin login requires a second factor; password-only admin login is not permitted.

option_description: Whether every admin account/management profile restricts access to a small permitted-IP/trusted-host set (FortiGate 'config system admin' trustedhostN; CIS PAN-OS 1.2.1/1.2.2 Permitted IP Addresses on each SSH/HTTPS/SNMP mgmt profile).
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Internet-exposed management plane with default or weak admin credentials" — when trustedhost is empty/0.0.0.0/0 or no permitted-IP list exists (FALSE), the admin plane accepts logins from any source (T1133 / T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read each FortiGate admin account's trustedhost entries.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each admin has trustedhost1..N set to specific mgmt subnets (e.g. 172.25.176.0/24); empty/0.0.0.0/0 trustedhost is insecure (FortiGate).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm Permitted IP Addresses are set on every mgmt profile that enables SSH/HTTPS/SNMP.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Network > Network Profiles > Interface Mgmt (Permitted IP Addresses per profile)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.2.1/1.2.2: 'Permitted IP Addresses' set on every interface-mgmt profile where SSH/HTTPS/SNMP is enabled, restricted to mgmt addresses only (Palo Alto).

option_description: Whether failed-login lockout/rate-limiting throttles brute-force against the management plane (FortiGate admin-lockout-threshold + admin-lockout-duration non-zero; CIS PAN-OS 1.4.2 Failed Attempts & Lockout Time non-zero).
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Internet-exposed management plane with default or weak admin credentials" — when lockout is disabled / attempts are unlimited (FALSE), unthrottled credential brute force succeeds (T1110).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the FortiGate global admin-lockout settings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: admin-lockout-threshold and admin-lockout-duration set to non-default hardened values (FortiGate).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm Failed Attempts and Lockout Time are configured non-zero in the Authentication Profile.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Device > Authentication Profile > (profile) > Advanced (Failed Attempts / Lockout Time)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.4.2: Failed Attempts & Lockout Time configured non-zero in the Authentication Profile (e.g. 3 attempts / 15 min) (Palo Alto).

option_description: Whether cleartext admin protocols HTTP or Telnet are permitted on any management interface (FortiOS allowaccess, CIS PAN 1.2.3-1.2.4). Secure posture allows only HTTPS + SSH.
security_impact: An is_true OR-trigger of the exposure "Cleartext / weak-TLS management transport" — when HTTP/Telnet admin is enabled (TRUE), admin credentials and config are exposed to sniffing/MITM on the management path (T1040 / T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the FortiGate interface allowaccess and confirm only https and ssh are listed.
how_to_obtain.command: config system interface / set allowaccess https ssh
how_to_obtain.expected_output: allowaccess lists only https ssh (no http, no telnet) — verify via 'show system interface' (FortiGate).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm HTTP and Telnet are unchecked on management interfaces/profiles.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Device > Setup > Management > Management Interface Settings (and Interface Mgmt profiles)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.2.3/1.2.4: HTTP and Telnet checkboxes UNCHECKED on management interfaces/profiles (Palo Alto).

option_description: Interpreted over the FortiOS admin-https-ssl-versions directive: TRUE when legacy SSL/TLS 1.0/1.1 are enabled for the admin HTTPS plane. Secure value is FALSE (TLS 1.2 minimum).
security_impact: An is_true OR-trigger of the exposure "Cleartext / weak-TLS management transport" — when legacy TLS 1.0/1.1 remain enabled (TRUE), the admin HTTPS plane is downgradeable to weak ciphers vulnerable to sniffing/MITM (T1040 / T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the FortiGate admin HTTPS TLS floor.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: admin-https-ssl-versions tlsv1-2 (or tlsv1-3) — not tlsv1-1/tlsv1-0 (FortiGate).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Handshake against the admin HTTPS port to confirm TLS 1.0/1.1 are refused.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLSv1.2 (and/or TLSv1.3) negotiated; TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 absent. TRUE (insecure) when TLS 1.0/1.1 negotiate.

option_description: Lowest TLS protocol version accepted on the management HTTPS plane (admin-https-ssl-versions floor). One of TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1/TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Cleartext / weak-TLS management transport" via the operator `in [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1]` — the management transport is weak when the negotiated floor is TLSv1.0 or TLSv1.1; the secure floor TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 does not fire (T1040).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the FortiGate admin-https-ssl-versions value, which expresses the negotiated floor.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: admin-https-ssl-versions tlsv1-2 (or tlsv1-3) — not tlsv1-1/tlsv1-0 (FortiGate). The floor maps to TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 (secure) vs TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 (fires).
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine the lowest version the admin HTTPS plane will negotiate on the wire.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect <appliance-mgmt-ip>:443 -tls1_1   # confirm it is refused
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS 1.1 handshake refused; lowest negotiable version is TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3.

option_description: Interpreted from admin-server-cert / the browser admin certificate (CIS PAN 1.2.5): TRUE when the management GUI presents a default self-signed (or expired) certificate rather than a valid CA-issued cert. Secure value is FALSE.
security_impact: An is_true OR-trigger of the exposure "Cleartext / weak-TLS management transport" — a default self-signed/expired cert (TRUE) prevents admins from detecting MITM on the management session (T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm the browser-based administrator certificate is from a trusted source and not self-signed.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Device > Certificate Management > Certificates / Device > Setup > Management (SSL/TLS Service Profile for admin)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.2.5: browser-based administrator certificate is from a trusted source, not self-signed, valid dates (Palo Alto).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the management GUI certificate off the wire and check issuer/validity.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Issuer is a trusted CA (not self-signed/issuer==subject) with current validity dates. TRUE (insecure) when self-signed or expired.

option_description: Whether the management TLS server certificate is validated against a trusted source (current validity dates, trusted issuer chain). Secure value is TRUE.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Cleartext / weak-TLS management transport" — when validation is absent (FALSE), the management session is open to certificate substitution/MITM (T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the management server certificate chain validity dates and trusted issuer.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Certificate has current validity dates and a trusted issuer chain. FALSE (insecure) when validation cannot be established.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm the admin certificate is from a trusted source with valid dates.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.2.5: browser-based administrator certificate is from a trusted source, not self-signed, valid dates (Palo Alto).

option_description: Interpreted from the SNMP polling configuration (CIS PAN 1.5.1): TRUE when community-based SNMP v1/v2c is enabled. Secure posture is SNMPv3-only.
security_impact: An is_true OR-trigger of the exposure "Cleartext / weak-TLS management transport" — community-based SNMP (TRUE) sends community strings across the management/monitoring plane in cleartext, exposing them to sniffing (T1040).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm the SNMP polling version is V3 and community-based versions are not used.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Device > Setup > Operations > SNMP Setup (Version V3)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.5.1: SNMP polling version V3 selected; community-based versions not used (Palo Alto).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On FortiGate, inspect the SNMP configuration for any v1/v2c community entries.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No v1/v2c community entries present; only SNMPv3 users configured. TRUE (insecure) when community entries exist.

option_description: Whether the firewall policy terminates in a default-deny (drop-all) posture so traffic not matched by an explicit allow rule is blocked (NIST SP 800-41 Rev.1). TRUE = default-deny (secure).
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Default-permit posture / no implicit-deny logging" — a default-permit/no-terminating-deny posture (FALSE) silently allows unintended traffic across the segmentation boundary (T1599).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the policy ordering and confirm the final/cleanup rule is a deny-all and no rule above it permits any/any.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Final/cleanup rule in the policy is a deny-all with logging; no rule above it permits 'any/any'. Posture defined from a risk analysis enumerating permitted protocols/ports.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-41 Rev.1 Guidelines on Firewalls and Firewall Policy

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the policy ruleset and inspect the terminating rule's action.
how_to_obtain.command: show firewall policy   # FortiOS; PAN-OS: show running security-policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Terminating/cleanup rule action is deny/drop; no broad any/any permit precedes it. FALSE (insecure) when no terminating deny exists.

option_description: Whether the implicit/terminating deny rule logs the traffic it drops, producing telemetry for detection and SIEM forwarding (NIST SP 800-41 Rev.1). TRUE = implicit deny logged (secure).
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Default-permit posture / no implicit-deny logging" — when the deny is not logged (FALSE), there is no telemetry on blocked attempts, a blind spot in segmentation enforcement (T1599).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm logging is enabled on the cleanup deny-all rule so dropped traffic is recorded.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Final/cleanup rule in the policy is a deny-all with logging; no rule above it permits 'any/any'. Posture defined from a risk analysis enumerating permitted protocols/ports.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-41 Rev.1 Guidelines on Firewalls and Firewall Policy

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the terminating deny rule's logging setting.
how_to_obtain.command: show firewall policy   # confirm 'set logtraffic all' on the deny rule (FortiOS)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The terminating deny rule has logging enabled (logtraffic all / Log at Session End). FALSE (insecure) when deny logging is off.

option_description: Whether the firewall forwards its logs off-box to a remote syslog/SIEM endpoint (CIS PAN 1.1.1.1 syslog profile with All Logs; CIS Controls v8 Control 8). FALSE means logs stay only on-device.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Insufficient traffic & admin logging to external SIEM" — without off-box forwarding (FALSE), firewall compromise/policy tampering goes undetected and on-box logs can be wiped (T1562.008 / T1562).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm a syslog profile points to a remote host with All Logs enabled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Device > Server Profiles > Syslog / Device > Log Settings (System, Configuration)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.1.1.1: Syslog profile points to a remote host with 'All Logs' enabled for System, Configuration, User-ID, HIP Match, IP-Tag (Palo Alto).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm logs are centralised off-device and present in the SIEM.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Logs centralised off-device; denied-traffic and admin-action events present in the SIEM (audit-log management process per CIS Control 8).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 — Control 8 Audit Log Management

option_description: Whether denied/dropped traffic (including the terminating implicit-deny) is logged and exported. FALSE removes telemetry on blocked attempts.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Insufficient traffic & admin logging to external SIEM" — when denied-traffic logging is off (FALSE), reconnaissance and policy-bypass attempts leave no record (T1562).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect deny/drop rules and confirm logtraffic is enabled, then confirm denied events reach the off-box collector.
how_to_obtain.command: show firewall policy   # confirm 'set logtraffic all' on deny rules (FortiOS)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Deny/drop rules log and denied traffic is exported off-box. FALSE (insecure) when deny logging is off.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On the SIEM, confirm denied/dropped traffic events from this firewall are present.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Denied-traffic events from the firewall appear in the SIEM (audit-log management process per CIS Control 8).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 — Control 8 Audit Log Management

option_description: Whether administrative/management-plane actions (logins, privileged operations) are captured and exported to the SIEM. FALSE means admin compromise goes unrecorded off-box.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Insufficient traffic & admin logging to external SIEM" — when admin-action logging is off (FALSE), unauthorized management-plane activity goes unrecorded off-box (T1562.008).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm System logs (admin login/operations) are forwarded to the syslog/SIEM profile.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.1.1.1: Syslog profile points to a remote host with 'All Logs' enabled for System, Configuration, User-ID, HIP Match, IP-Tag (Palo Alto).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On the SIEM, confirm admin login and privileged-operation events from the firewall are present.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Admin logins and privileged operations are logged and forwarded off-box (audit-log management per CIS Control 8).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 — Control 8 Audit Log Management

option_description: Whether firewall configuration-change events (ruleset/policy edits) are logged and exported off-box (CIS PAN System/Configuration logs). FALSE means policy tampering produces no retained record.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Insufficient traffic & admin logging to external SIEM" — when config-change logging is off (FALSE), silently relaxing the ruleset produces no detectable, retained record (T1562.008).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm Configuration logs are forwarded to the syslog/SIEM profile.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.1.1.1: Syslog profile points to a remote host with 'All Logs' enabled for System, Configuration, User-ID, HIP Match, IP-Tag (Palo Alto).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On the SIEM, confirm configuration/system change events from the firewall are present.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration/system change events are logged and exported to the SIEM (audit-log management per CIS Control 8).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 — Control 8 Audit Log Management

option_description: Whether traffic crossing the network perimeter the firewall enforces is logged and centralized to a common store/SIEM. FALSE means boundary crossings are not observable centrally.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Insufficient traffic & admin logging to external SIEM" — when crossings are not centralized (FALSE), cross-system correlation of an attack against the segmentation device is defeated (T1562).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm perimeter-crossing traffic logs are centralized to a common SIEM/log store.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Logs centralised off-device; denied-traffic and admin-action events present in the SIEM (audit-log management process per CIS Control 8).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 — Control 8 Audit Log Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: On the SIEM, confirm traffic logs for boundary crossings from this firewall are indexed centrally.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Perimeter-crossing traffic events from the firewall are present and queryable in the central SIEM. FALSE (insecure) when not centralized.

option_description: Whether logs are stored on a system separate from the firewall that generates them, so a device compromise cannot also delete the evidence. FALSE means on-device-only retention.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Insufficient traffic & admin logging to external SIEM" — on-device-only retention (FALSE) lets an attacker who compromises the device also wipe the evidence (T1562.008).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a copy of logs is retained on a system independent of the firewall.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Logs centralised off-device; denied-traffic and admin-action events present in the SIEM (audit-log management process per CIS Control 8).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 — Control 8 Audit Log Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm a remote syslog destination exists so logs are not retained only locally.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.1.1.1: Syslog profile points to a remote host with 'All Logs' enabled (Palo Alto) — off-box copy exists.

option_description: Whether retained audit logs are tamper-evident (write-once / integrity-protected) so on-device wiping or alteration is detectable. FALSE means logs can be silently wiped/edited.
security_impact: A secondary is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Insufficient traffic & admin logging to external SIEM" — when logs are not tamper-evident (FALSE), they can be silently wiped or edited after a firewall compromise (T1562.008).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm retained logs are write-once or integrity-protected so tampering is detectable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Off-box log store is write-once / integrity-protected (e.g. WORM/immutable retention); tampering is detectable. FALSE (insecure) when logs are freely editable.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 — Control 8 Audit Log Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the SIEM/log-store retention configuration for immutability/integrity controls.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Retention policy enforces immutability or cryptographic integrity on stored firewall logs.

option_description: Whether the firewall enforces session/connection-table protection — per-source and global session limits, SYN-flood / new-connection-rate thresholds — so a flood cannot exhaust the global session table or CPU. TRUE = caps/thresholds in place.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Firewall self-DoS / connection-table exhaustion with fail-open" — without session-table limits (FALSE), a flood can exhaust the connection table and drop legitimate traffic (T1499.002 / T1499.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify DoS-protection or session-limit policies (per-source/global caps, SYN-flood thresholds) are applied on the appliance/zones.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DoS-protection / session-limit policies (per-source/global caps, SYN-flood thresholds) applied. FALSE (insecure) when no session-table limits exist.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect DoS-protection policy on the appliance.
how_to_obtain.command: show firewall DoS-policy   # FortiOS; PAN-OS: review Policies > DoS Protection
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DoS-protection policy present with session/connection thresholds bound to ingress zones.

option_description: Whether anti-DDoS/flood-protection controls (rate limiting, SYN-cookie / aggregate flood thresholds, or upstream/scrubbing protection) defend the device against volumetric and protocol floods. TRUE = protection present.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Firewall self-DoS / connection-table exhaustion with fail-open" — without anti-flood protection (FALSE), the device is unprotected against floods aimed at exhausting its capacity (T1498.001 / T1499).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm anti-flood/DDoS controls (rate limits, SYN-cookies, scrubbing) protect the device.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Anti-flood/DDoS controls (rate limits, SYN-cookies, or upstream scrubbing) present. FALSE (insecure) when the device is unprotected against floods.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect SYN-flood / flood-protection thresholds on the appliance.
how_to_obtain.command: show firewall DoS-policy   # FortiOS anomaly/flood thresholds; PAN-OS: Zone Protection profile flood settings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Flood-protection (SYN-cookie / aggregate thresholds) configured on ingress zones, or an upstream scrubbing service documented.

option_description: Whether the device's behaviour under resource exhaustion/overload is fail-OPEN (passes traffic unfiltered when the session table fills or CPU saturates). TRUE (insecure) = fails open; FALSE = fails closed.
security_impact: An is_true OR-trigger of the exposure "Firewall self-DoS / connection-table exhaustion with fail-open" — fail-open under overload (TRUE) silently removes the enforcement boundary when resources are exhausted (T1499.001 / T1498.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine the device's documented overload behaviour and confirm the configured fail-safe stance.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Device fails closed / has a defined fail-safe stance that preserves enforcement under overload. TRUE (insecure) when traffic passes unfiltered when resources are exhausted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the fail-to-wire / bypass setting on inline/transparent interfaces.
how_to_obtain.command: show system global   # check fail-open/bypass behaviour; review HW bypass on inline pairs
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Inline/transparent interfaces configured fail-closed (no hardware bypass passing traffic) under overload.

option_description: Whether the firewall runs as an HA pair with session synchronization and link/path monitoring so a single device failure (or a flood that downs one unit) does not collapse the enforcement boundary. TRUE = HA with session sync + monitoring.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Firewall self-DoS / connection-table exhaustion with fail-open" — a single non-HA device / no link monitoring (FALSE) amplifies availability impact under a flood (T1498.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm HA session sync, link/path monitoring and preemption settings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Device > High Availability (HA2 Session Synchronization; Link and Path Monitoring; Election Settings)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 3.1: Session Synchronization on HA2 enabled; CIS 3.2: Link/Path Monitoring enabled with Failure Condition 'Any'; CIS 3.3: Preemptive disabled (Palo Alto).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On FortiGate, confirm the HA cluster status, session sync and monitored interfaces.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HA cluster present (a-p/a-a) with session-pickup enabled and monitored interfaces. FALSE (insecure) when a single standalone device with no monitoring.

option_description: Whether the NGFW's IPS/threat-prevention engine is active and inspecting traffic (PAN-OS WildFire/Threat-Prevention engine running, FortiGate IPS/AV engine enabled). FALSE means the firewall is a blind passthrough.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Inspection disabled / stale signatures enabling evasion" — when the engine is disabled (FALSE), the firewall is a blind passthrough that bridges the trusted/untrusted boundary uninspected (T1599 / T1562).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm a WildFire/threat-prevention profile is active and inspection is running.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Objects > Security Profiles > Vulnerability Protection / Anti-Spyware (engine status via Dashboard)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 5.3: WildFire/threat-prevention profile enabled on all security policies with an Allow action (Palo Alto). Engine actively inspecting.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On FortiGate, confirm the IPS/AV engine is enabled and inspecting.
how_to_obtain.command: diagnose test application ipsmonitor 1   # IPS engine status (FortiOS)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IPS/AV engine running and processing traffic. FALSE (insecure) when the engine is disabled.

option_description: Whether IPS/AV/application-and-threat content signatures are current (content auto-update enabled and recently applied per CIS Palo Alto 4.1/4.2; FortiGuard content current). FALSE means signatures are stale/manual.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Inspection disabled / stale signatures enabling evasion" — stale signatures (FALSE) let the engine miss known threats even while running (T1562).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm AV and Applications-and-Threats content are set to Download and Install on a frequent schedule and recently applied.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Device > Dynamic Updates (Antivirus, Applications and Threats schedules / last-installed)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 1.6.1: 'Verify Update Server Identity' checked; CIS 4.1/4.2: AV and Applications-and-Threats set to Download and Install on a frequent schedule (Palo Alto).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On FortiGate, confirm FortiGuard IPS/AV content versions are current.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IPS/AV signature packages at the latest FortiGuard version with recent contract update timestamps. FALSE (insecure) when stale.

option_description: Whether every security policy with an Allow action has a threat-prevention/security profile (IPS, AV, anti-spyware, WildFire/sandboxing) attached so permitted traffic is actually inspected. FALSE means Allow rules pass traffic uninspected.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Inspection disabled / stale signatures enabling evasion" — Allow rules without profiles (FALSE) pass traffic without inspection even when the engine runs (T1599 / T1562).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm every Allow security policy has a threat-prevention/WildFire profile attached.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Policies > Security (Profile column on each Allow rule)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CIS 5.3: WildFire/threat-prevention profile enabled on all security policies with an Allow action (Palo Alto).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On FortiGate, inspect allow policies for attached UTM/security profiles.
how_to_obtain.command: show firewall policy   # confirm ips-sensor / av-profile set on action accept rules (FortiOS)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every accept policy references an IPS sensor / AV / application-control profile. FALSE (insecure) when allow rules have no profile.

option_description: Whether SSL/TLS decryption-and-inspection is applied to traffic crossing the boundary (where policy and privacy allow) so encrypted threats are not a blind spot. FALSE means encrypted traffic passes uninspected.
security_impact: A secondary is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Inspection disabled / stale signatures enabling evasion" — without TLS inspection (FALSE), TLS-wrapped malware/C2 and evasion cross the boundary uninspected (T1599).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On PAN-OS, confirm an SSL forward-proxy / decryption policy decrypts and inspects traffic where policy permits.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An SSL forward-proxy / TLS inspection policy decrypts and inspects traffic where policy permits. FALSE (insecure) when encrypted traffic passes uninspected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On FortiGate, inspect policies for a deep-inspection SSL profile.
how_to_obtain.command: show firewall policy   # confirm ssl-ssh-profile set to a deep-inspection profile (FortiOS)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Relevant policies reference a deep-inspection (not certificate-inspection-only) SSL profile where policy/privacy allow.

option_description: Whether changes to the firewall configuration are detected and recorded through a change-control workflow (NIST CM-3). TRUE when every config edit is captured against a tracked baseline.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Unauthorized config drift without change control" — ad-hoc unattributed rule edits (FALSE) let unauthorized rule changes silently weaken segmentation undetected (T1562.004 / T1562.013).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm config edits flow through a change-control workflow and are captured against a tracked baseline.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented, version-controlled, reviewed baseline (CM-2) with a change-control workflow (CM-3) and restricted change access (CM-5) for the firewall config.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Configuration Management (CM) family

how_to_obtain.instruction: On the SIEM, confirm config-change events are recorded and attributable to a change ticket.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration-change events present and tied to a change-control record. FALSE (insecure) when edits are ad-hoc and unattributed.

option_description: Whether the running firewall config is automatically compared against a reviewed, version-controlled baseline to surface drift. TRUE when drift is detected and alerted.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Unauthorized config drift without change control" — with no drift detection (FALSE), malicious or accidental rule changes are undetectable (T1562.004).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm automated comparison of the running config against a version-controlled baseline with drift alerting.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented, version-controlled, reviewed baseline (CM-2) with a change-control workflow (CM-3) and restricted change access (CM-5) for the firewall config.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Configuration Management (CM) family

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the config-management tooling (e.g. Panorama/FortiManager diff, or a NCCM tool) for scheduled drift comparison and alerting.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Tooling periodically diffs running config vs baseline and alerts on drift. FALSE (insecure) when no drift detection exists.

option_description: Whether the device's currently running configuration matches the approved version-controlled baseline (NIST CM-2). TRUE when running config equals the reviewed baseline.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Unauthorized config drift without change control" — when uncontrolled drift is present (FALSE), the live ruleset diverges from the authorized segmentation policy (T1562.013).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Compare the running configuration against the approved version-controlled baseline.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented, version-controlled, reviewed baseline (CM-2) with a change-control workflow (CM-3) and restricted change access (CM-5) for the firewall config.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Configuration Management (CM) family

how_to_obtain.instruction: Export the running config and diff it against the stored baseline.
how_to_obtain.command: show full-configuration   # FortiOS export; PAN-OS: 'show config running' / Panorama config diff
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Running config equals the reviewed baseline (empty diff). FALSE (insecure) when uncontrolled drift is present.

option_description: Whether the firewall configuration is regularly backed up off-box to a known-good, tamper-evident store. TRUE when off-box backups exist and are verified.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Unauthorized config drift without change control" — with no off-box backup (FALSE), a maliciously altered config is unrecoverable (T1562.004).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm regular, verified off-box backups of the configuration to a known-good store.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented, version-controlled, reviewed baseline (CM-2) with a change-control workflow (CM-3) and restricted change access (CM-5) for the firewall config.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Configuration Management (CM) family

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the backup schedule and a recent restore-test record for the firewall config store.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Off-box config backups taken on a schedule and verified by restore test. FALSE (insecure) when no off-box backup exists.

option_description: Whether out-of-band (direct CLI/GUI) edits bypassing the change-control workflow are prevented or detected via restricted change access (NIST CM-5). TRUE when OOB changes are blocked or reconciled.
security_impact: An is_false OR-trigger of the exposure "Unauthorized config drift without change control" — when admins can edit rules ad-hoc with no control (FALSE), silent unauthorized rule changes are permitted (T1562.013).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm direct CLI/GUI edits are blocked or reconciled against the change-control workflow.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented, version-controlled, reviewed baseline (CM-2) with a change-control workflow (CM-3) and restricted change access (CM-5) for the firewall config.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Configuration Management (CM) family

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review whether direct device access is restricted (e.g. config pushed only from Panorama/FortiManager) and OOB edits are reconciled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Direct device edits are blocked or automatically reconciled to the management plane of record. FALSE (insecure) when ad-hoc edits go uncontrolled.
